university: University of Texas at San Antonio

documents.title: From Imagination to Implementation: Using Generative AI in Teaching and Learning (UTSA faculty GenAI guidelines)
tiers: authorized only as a virtual learning assistant
documents.summary: UTSA's Academic Innovation office publishes a faculty guide to generative AI in teaching, learning and research. It sets no student-facing AI rule; it tells each instructor to state in the syllabus whether and how AI is allowed, offers three example positions, and adds advice on privacy, detection, citation, assessment design, career preparation and research use.
documents.stance_why: The guide says "Faculty are responsible for their syllabus and courses" and "You always have control over your course", and lists three options (encourage, "authorized only as a virtual learning assistant", "not authorized"). It sets no university-wide default, so the stance is delegates with those three tiers.

units.why: The preamble says UTSA is "committed to assisting and partnering with faculty to integrate AI"; this is an institution-level statement of purpose, so P56, general, informs.
units.anchor: committed to assisting and partnering with faculty to integrate AI

units.why: "We must also anticipate how to prepare current and future students who will encounter AI in their personal and professional lives" gives a career-readiness reason to engage with AI, so P44.
units.anchor: prepare current and future students who will encounter AI in their personal and professional lives

units.why: The guide was "created" by "a team of UTSA faculty and staff members, part of the UTSA AI Peer Learning Network"; it says who drafted the guidance, so P84.
units.anchor: A team of UTSA faculty and staff members, part of the UTSA AI Peer

units.why: "these guidelines will be reviewed and refreshed annually" commits to a review cycle, so P54.
units.anchor: these guidelines will be reviewed and refreshed annually

units.why: "We will continue to seek feedback to inform these guidelines" invites feedback and treats the guide as a starting point, so P54 (separate from the annual review sentence).
units.anchor: We will continue to seek feedback to inform these guidelines

units.why: "Our approach reflects our commitment to fostering innovation while respecting individual choices" leaves AI decisions to individual faculty, so P04.
units.anchor: fostering innovation while respecting individual choices

units.why: Faculty "explore various generative AI tools' potential benefits and shortcomings to see how they align with and advance the faculty's learning objectives"; the choice follows learning objectives, so P83.
units.anchor: how they align with and advance the faculty's learning objectives
units.policy: Faculty are encouraged to explore generative AI tools' potential benefits and shortcomings to see how they align with and advance the faculty's learning objectives.

units.why: The "human-centered approach ... focusing on student growth, ethical responsibility, and meaningful engagement" is a framing principle for the guide, so P56.
units.anchor: we emphasize a human-centered approach to integrating generative AI in teaching and learning

units.why: "we encourage students to reflect on the ethical implications of AI use" asks for ethical reflection; closest is P53 but it names no specific harm.
units.anchor: we encourage students to reflect on the ethical implications of AI use
units.fit_note: Encourages reflection on ethics generally; names no specific bias, labor or environmental harm.

units.why: Under "How can I use Generative AI?" it lists "personalized and interactive content tailored to individual learning styles"; this names a benefit of AI, so P87.
units.anchor: providing personalized and interactive content tailored to individual learning styles and needs

units.why: "saving time on administrative tasks such as emails, course announcements" is an instructor use of AI for teaching work, so P59.
units.anchor: saving time on administrative tasks such as emails, course announcements

units.why: "Foster new forms of creative and critical thinking as well as problem-solving skills using AI tools" names a learning benefit, so P87 (no career claim, so not P44).
units.anchor: new forms of creative and critical thinking as well as problem-solving skills using AI tools

units.why: "Create content in different formats to meet the needs of all learners" is an instructor use of AI for course materials, so P59.
units.anchor: Create content in different formats to meet the needs of all learners

units.why: "Create rubrics, assessment questions, and learning objectives" lists instructor uses of AI, so P59.
units.anchor: Create rubrics, assessment questions, and learning objectives

units.why: "Provide students with constructive, formative feedback" is an instructor use of AI for feedback; it is a use, not a conditional grading rule, so P59 rather than P101.
units.anchor: Generative AI can help identify areas for improvement

units.why: "Prompt self-reflection, encouraging students to critically evaluate their use of AI" asks instructors to build reflection into the course, so P35; no reflection submission is required, so P26 does not fit.
units.anchor: encouraging students to critically evaluate their use of AI and its impact
units.fit_note: Suggests instructors prompt reflection on AI use; no required submission is stated.

units.why: "Promote critical thinking, guiding students to analyze, question, and assess information generated by AI" asks that AI output be evaluated critically, so P31.
units.anchor: guiding students to analyze, question, and assess information generated by AI

units.why: "always disclose your approach to AI integration, the factors considered ... and your rationale" is an instructor duty to disclose to students, so P47.
units.anchor: always disclose your approach to AI integration
units.fit_note: Disclosure covers the approach and rationale for adopting AI, not only the instructor's own use.

units.why: "It is critical to educate your students about data privacy and the potential risks associated with sharing personal information" tells instructors to teach privacy, so P50.
units.anchor: educate your students about data privacy and the potential risks associated with sharing personal information

units.why: "AI is a tool to enhance, not replace, the educator's role" states a principle on AI and teaching, so P56.
units.anchor: AI is a tool to enhance, not replace, the educator's role
units.policy: AI is a tool to enhance, not replace, the educator's role in facilitating meaningful learning experiences.

units.why: "Students should use caution when using AI platforms and embrace a continuous learning mindset" asks students to stay informed, so P102, plus a caution element.
units.anchor: embrace a continuous learning mindset to make informed decisions
units.fit_note: Also asks for caution with AI platforms, which P102 does not capture.

units.why: "Suggest your students use AI-enabled search engines to help find the underlying sources of their AI responses" advises a verification practice, so P31.
units.anchor: use AI-enabled search engines to help find the underlying sources of their AI responses

units.why: "they must provide a secondary citation to verify their AI response's content and correctly attribute it" requires verifying citations, so P31 rather than P24 because the point is confirming content.
units.anchor: provide a secondary citation to verify their AI response's content and correctly
units.fit_note: Also requires attribution of the AI response, which touches P24.

units.why: "Demonstrate how to check AI responses for bias with sample artifacts" tells instructors to model bias checking, so P31 (AI output can be biased; verify).
units.anchor: Demonstrate how to check AI responses for bias with sample artifacts

units.why: "This is the only UTSA-approved AI tool" names Microsoft CoPilot as the one approved, university-licensed tool for everyone; it is institution-wide, so P92 not P17.
units.anchor: Microsoft CoPilot license to get started with generative AI

units.why: "commercial data protection ... data are not used to train foundational LLMs" explains why CoPilot is vetted, a data-protection fact, so P50.
units.anchor: responses and data are not used to train foundational LLMs
units.policy: This is the only UTSA-approved AI tool because it offers the power of GPT-4 with Microsoft's stringent commercial data protection, so responses and data are not used to train foundational LLMs.

units.why: "Users should be careful to avoid sharing private data to any LLM" cautions all users, so P50.
units.anchor: Users should be careful to avoid sharing private data to any LLM

units.why: Adobe Creative Cloud users "can also use the generative AI features" in Express and Firefly, a second university-provided tool, so P92.
units.anchor: can also use the generative AI features enabled in apps such as Adobe Creative Express

units.why: "AI can generate alternative text for images, aiding visually impaired students" presents AI as an accessibility aid, so P97.
units.anchor: AI can generate alternative text for images, aiding visually impaired students

units.why: "AI can personalize learning experiences by analyzing individual student interactions" states a benefit of AI, so P87.
units.anchor: AI can personalize learning experiences by analyzing individual student interactions

units.why: "Add AI and Data Privacy to your syllabus and course homepage" tells instructors to put privacy information in the syllabus, so P09.
units.anchor: Add AI and Data Privacy to your syllabus and course homepage
units.fit_note: Concerns an AI and data privacy statement rather than the AI-use rule.

units.why: "Review the sign-on and data privacy policies for the various AI platforms" is privacy advice for students, so P50.
units.anchor: Review the sign-on and data privacy policies for the various AI platforms

units.why: "enable this option to add an extra layer of security" advises 2FA on AI accounts, account security advice, so P50.
units.anchor: If the generative AI platform offers two-factor authentication (2FA), enable this option
units.frag_end: extra layer of security to your account.
units.fit_note: Account-security advice; P50 centers on personal data and vetted tools.

units.why: "Use generic or fictional data when generating content to prevent the exposure of personal or sensitive information" is privacy advice for prompts, so P50.
units.anchor: Use generic or fictional data when generating content

units.why: "Clear your browser cache and cookies regularly to minimize the collection of browsing history" is privacy hygiene advice, so P50 at best.
units.anchor: Clear your browser cache and cookies regularly
units.fit_note: General browsing-privacy hygiene, not specific to prompts or vetted tools.

units.why: "foster an open dialogue with your students and encourage them to share any questions or concerns" asks instructors who use AI to discuss it with students, so P66.
units.anchor: foster an open dialogue with your students and encourage them to share

units.why: "Consider collaborating with ... Academic Innovation to analyze and measure the impact of AI on your students' learning" invites evidence gathering, so P55.
units.anchor: analyze and measure the impact of AI on your students' learning

units.why: "book a consultation with the Teaching, Learning and Digital Transformation team" offers faculty support, so P63.
units.anchor: book a consultation with the Teaching, Learning and Digital Transformation team

units.why: "Faculty are responsible for their syllabus and courses" and "may choose different approaches" means each instructor sets the rule, so P04.
units.anchor: Because faculty may choose different approaches for generative AI
units.frag_end: whether and how you are allowing the use of AI.
units.policy: Faculty are responsible for their syllabus and courses, and may choose different approaches for generative AI.

units.why: "clearly state in the syllabus and the course homepage whether and how you are allowing the use of AI" is a direction to state AI expectations, so P09.
units.anchor: clearly state in the syllabus and the course homepage whether and how
units.policy: Faculty clearly state in the syllabus and the course homepage whether and how they allow the use of AI.
units.fit_note: Imperative in guidance; modality read as must.

units.why: "You always have control over your course" affirms instructor discretion including opting out, so P04.
units.anchor: You always have control over your course

units.why: The example statements "encouraged ... authorized only as a virtual learning assistant ... not authorized" are three named positions instructors can pick, so P05.
units.anchor: Use of generative AI is authorized only as a virtual learning assistant
units.policy: Example syllabus statements: AI use is encouraged to complete assignments; authorized only as a virtual learning assistant; or not authorized.
units.fit_note: A three-option menu of syllabus statements rather than named tiers.

units.why: "inherently imperfect and prone to false positives and false negatives" says detectors are unreliable, so P39.
units.anchor: these tools are inherently imperfect and prone to false positives and false negatives

units.why: The guide favors "evidence-based evaluations and open communication with students rather than depending solely on AI detection results", an evidence standard, so P69.
units.anchor: evidence-based evaluations and open communication with students rather than depending solely on AI detection results

units.why: "we emphasize following the established processes and guidelines outlined in the university's code of conduct" sends AI concerns to the existing integrity process, so P36.
units.anchor: following the established processes and guidelines outlined in the university's code of conduct
units.fit_note: Routes suspected AI misuse to the code of conduct without calling it misconduct outright.

units.why: "students the option to demonstrate their knowledge in ways that do not encourage AI use" is an assessment redesign, so P35.
units.anchor: students the option to demonstrate their knowledge in ways that do not encourage AI use

units.why: "Deepening your digital and AI literacy skills by reviewing the resources" asks faculty to learn about AI, so P63.
units.anchor: Deepening your digital and AI literacy skills by reviewing the resources

units.why: "Creating assignments that encourage students to demonstrate higher-level thinking that AI cannot generate, such as reflections" is assessment redesign, so P35.
units.anchor: assignments that encourage students to demonstrate higher-level thinking that AI cannot generate

units.why: "Teaching students to use generative AI as a tool for deeper learning" recommends teaching AI use, so P44.
units.anchor: Teaching students to use generative AI as a tool for deeper learning

units.why: "Sharing UTSA policies regarding academic integrity and conduct with students" tells instructors to communicate integrity policies; nearest is P66, which is about explaining rules.
units.anchor: Sharing UTSA policies regarding academic integrity and conduct with students
units.fit_note: Sharing existing integrity policies with students rather than explaining AI rules.

units.why: "Setting expectations with students about the use of AI in your course" recommends communicating expectations, so P09.
units.anchor: Setting expectations with students about the use of AI in your course

units.why: "We recommend that students attribute and properly cite generative AI when it is used for text or images" recommends citation, so P24 with modality should.
units.anchor: We recommend that students attribute and properly cite generative AI
units.policy: The guide recommends that students attribute and properly cite generative AI when it is used for text or images.

units.why: "Refer to the APA guidelines for proper citation and attribution" points to named AI citation formats, so P25 loosely.
units.anchor: Refer to the APA guidelines for proper citation and attribution
units.fit_note: Points to APA and MLA citation guides; does not itself require tool, prompt or date.

units.why: "Clarify the expectations for TAs and Graders regarding the use of AI" tells instructors to set AI rules for TAs, so P09 aimed at staff.
units.anchor: Clarify the expectations for TAs and Graders regarding the use of AI
units.fit_note: Applies to expectations for TAs and graders, not students.

units.why: "simulations in use cases to show how to demonstrate learning without relying on AI" is assessment design, so P35.
units.anchor: simulations in use cases to show how to demonstrate learning without relying on AI

units.why: "Provide examples of activities and assignments that do not promote AI use, or that promote an ethical use of AI" asks instructors to model options, so P35.
units.anchor: Provide examples of activities and assignments that do not promote AI use

units.why: The conduct resources name the "Office of the Dean of Students"; it lists offices that handle misconduct, so P80 loosely.
units.anchor: UTSA Office of the Dean of Students
units.fit_note: Lists resources and offices; does not state who enforces an AI policy.

units.why: "strike a balance that upholds academic integrity while harnessing the benefits of technology" is a principle for the guide, so P56.
units.anchor: strike a balance that upholds academic integrity while harnessing the benefits of technology

units.why: Faculty "should take into account traditional results ... but also measure the development of foundational skills" asks for broader measurement of learning, so P55 loosely.
units.anchor: also measure the development of foundational skills
units.fit_note: Asks faculty to measure foundational skills alongside grades; not framed as AI-impact evidence.

units.why: "clearly defining academic integrity expectations and designing assignments with specific" ties assessment to objectives, so P35.
units.anchor: clearly defining academic integrity expectations and designing assignments with specific

units.why: "integrating AI as a supplement to teaching rather than as a substitute is crucial" is an instructor-facing principle, so P56.
units.anchor: integrating AI as a supplement to teaching rather than as a substitute is crucial

units.why: "Crafting assignments to discourage shortcut solutions" is assessment redesign, so P35.
units.anchor: Crafting assignments to discourage shortcut solutions

units.why: "faculty members should provide clear expectations and rationale for when AI might not be the optimal choice" tells instructors to explain their rules, so P66.
units.anchor: provide clear expectations and rationale for when AI might not be the optimal choice

units.why: AI should serve "without overshadowing the critical thinking, writing, and analytical skills essential for lifelong success", a skill-building reason for limits, so P41.
units.anchor: without overshadowing the critical thinking, writing, and analytical skills essential for lifelong success
units.fit_note: Frames AI as a complement that must not overshadow skills; does not say practice is outsourced.

units.why: "incorporate a statement in their syllabi that reflects how they expect students" asks for an AI syllabus statement, so P09.
units.anchor: incorporate a statement in their syllabi that reflects how they expect students

units.why: The three options "Encourage all students to fully embrace", "Allow ... only in certain circumstances", "Not allow ... in any form" are named positions, so P05.
units.anchor: Allow the use of generative AI only in certain circumstances, activities or assignments
units.frag_end: in any form in the course.
units.policy: Faculty can encourage all students to fully embrace generative AI, allow it only in certain circumstances, activities or assignments as set out in the syllabus and assignment instructions, or not allow it in any form in the course.
units.fit_note: Three options for instructors; the middle option is also restrict-like.

units.why: "For sample language to use in their syllabi, faculty can visit" points to sample statements, a template resource, so P09 loosely.
units.anchor: For sample language to use in their syllabi, faculty can visit
units.fit_note: Offers sample statements rather than requiring a statement.

units.why: "design assignments with specific learning objectives that discourage shortcut solutions" in the Design Assessment Strategies list is assessment redesign, so P35.
units.anchor: design assignments with specific learning objectives that discourage shortcut solutions

units.why: "asking students to document how they used AI tools, what specific prompts" is assignment design for prompt documentation, so P26.
units.anchor: asking students to document how they used AI tools, what specific prompts

units.why: "reflective components where students analyze the ethical implications of AI use" adds ethics reflection to assignments, so P35.
units.anchor: reflective components where students analyze the ethical implications of AI use

units.why: "work with them to identify alternative ways to engage with the assignment" offers alternatives to students with ethical objections, so P51.
units.anchor: work with them to identify alternative ways to engage with the assignment

units.why: "Conducting manual or traditional research instead of using AI" is one listed non-AI route for students who object, so P51.
units.anchor: Conducting manual or traditional research instead of using AI for ideation

units.why: "human-machine collaboration will likely become the status quo" is a careers reason to engage with AI, so P44.
units.anchor: human-machine collaboration will likely become the status quo

units.why: "foster familiarity and proficiency with generative AI platforms" and "a marketable advantage" state AI skill as employer-valued, so P44.
units.anchor: foster familiarity and proficiency with generative AI platforms

units.why: "It will be imperative that students know and understand how AI tools can be used in their chosen career field" says students must learn AI for careers, so P44.
units.anchor: students know and understand how AI tools can be used in their chosen career field

units.why: "Authors must be transparent to the journal and the paper's co-authors in disclosing the use of generative AI tools" is a research disclosure rule, so P62.
units.anchor: Authors must be transparent to the journal and the paper's co-authors

units.why: "Authors are responsible for checking the accuracy of the AI-generated outputs" puts verification on researchers, so P62 (research context) rather than P31.
units.anchor: Authors are responsible for checking the accuracy of the AI-generated outputs

units.why: "Generative AI can help create outlines or summaries" permits a research use within limits, so P62.
units.anchor: Generative AI can help create outlines or summaries within the limitations

units.why: "may be prohibited in many cases. Check the specific journal or grant application requirements" defers to venue and funder rules, so P62.
units.anchor: Check the specific journal or grant application requirements before using any AI tool

units.why: "Never upload your grant application (novel idea) into any AI tool" bans uploading research documents, so P62 rather than P49 (course materials).
units.anchor: Never upload your grant application (novel idea) into any AI tool

units.why: "Researchers should always check with the sponsoring agency regarding their policies" defers to sponsor rules on peer review, so P62.
units.anchor: Researchers should always check with the sponsoring agency regarding their policies

units.why: NIH "has prohibited scientific peer reviewers from employing ... large language models" is cited as an example sponsor ban, so P62.
units.anchor: prohibited scientific peer reviewers from employing natural language processors, large language models

units.why: "composing critiques or improving grammar and syntax is also regarded as a breach of confidentiality" extends the peer review ban, so P62.
units.anchor: composing critiques or improving grammar and syntax is also regarded as a breach of confidentiality

units.why: The online faculty course and "peer learning community" are professional development for instructors, so P63.
units.anchor: online self-paced course to introduce faculty to generative AI and create a peer learning community

notes: Single university-level faculty guide. No school, computing or course documents collected. Several units fit types only partly (see fit_note).
